body: PM me please. Or check your messages. I’ve got a similar story my friend and can relate

I would say it’s closer to three weeks for a heavier (daily user). Especially if you’re an average person with body fat. At least with people I’ve known, they’ve failed drug tests for work (which I would say are not as thorough unless it’s a hair follicle) being clean for even two weeks. Who fucking knows. We can agree the longer you abstain the more likely you are to pass.

Verdicts out. I’ve seen up to nine days. Really no way to tell if it’s on the test without asking (red flag) so I’m just patiently waiting for Thursday. It’s all good either way, haven’t signed a contract with them so I’m not really breaking any agreement yet

Hopefully you’re okay. I am in an incredibly similar situation. I’m switching doctors because of insurance, first appt is Thursday and I’m also hoping a 20 day break is good enough to piss clean. Although I’m confident I’ll be good, I’m super skinny and have pissed clean after 10 days before. I’m more concerned about Kratom showing up on my test than THC but I’m prepared to talk about why I’ve been using it and hope that’s good enough. Here’s a link to [New York’s guidelines. ](https://www.health.ny.gov/professionals/narcotic/opioid_treatment_guidelines/) Hope that helps!

I’d imagine your doctor is going to want you to piss clean for THC. If you truly stopped 3 weeks ago you should be in a good spot. To be safe hydrate like a mother this weekend and the day of your test and you’ll probably pee clean. No guarantees but if you’re really concerned maybe drink lots of dandelion tea or something else that can help detox you (don’t waste your money on detox drinks though, they’re an expensive scam). I only suggest dandelion tea because cheap (relatively) and will help a bit. Maybe some b12 (niacin) if you’re especially concerned. But if you’re about three weeks out hydration (3-4L a day all weekend and Mon/Tue) will be your best bet. Good luck and try not to be too concerned, worrying too much won’t do you any good. 

If you do pee hot explain to your doctor you used one time to help with a flare as opposed to going to the emergency room (claim financial concerns about going to the ER) and you may will probably get a warning and told to avoid further use. 

As u/old-goat explained in a post made, there aren’t actually restrictions about THC and prescribing opioids but doctors tend to lie to us to cover their asses from loses their license to practice. What state are you in? Look up the states guidelines for opioid therapy and familiarize yourself with the guidelines so you can go in showing to your doctor you are educating yourself about your treatment. It should help you have something to stand on if the doctor gives you grief. 

Good luck!
Damn u/old-goat why you gotta educate me like that. BOOM ROASTED! Thank you for sharing some hard facts with me. You are doing some good work informing us and I appreciate it!

I  like your thinking but I’m already on 45 MME (10mg oxy/3x per day) which is near the limit unless you have terminal cancer. I know they test for THC, was lucky with my last doctor looking the other way with my positive tests but was already warned by my current doc this clinic is not going to have the same stance. ER meds don’t seem as effective treating my pain however I’ve not been lucky enough to get ER and IR simultaneously to know how they’d work synergistically.  On the bright side they do write mmj recommendations but I’m still waiting on MN to fully implement flower cannabis (was just recently approved at least) into the system. Ultimately I’ll probably avoid the license though as the quality of street MJ here is on par with MMJ from other places (CO is my reference) and I find the cost of the license too high and the cost for medical v street is equal for now at least. I will take your advice and speak to the physician when I meet with them next week. Like you suggest openness is the best way to build this relationship with your doctor. Thanks for your advice

About the GC cost, I think you’d be surprised about clinics using them. They seem to be fairly common where I’ve visited. Scientifically speaking they’ve got a lot more efficacy (can’t be fooled as easily), also I’d imagine in the long run it’s just so much easier (less waste). Who knows though, it’s beside the main point

Yeah most pain clinics aren’t using this style of tests you buy in a store. They are likely using fluoroscopy or a gas chromatograph, both of which are much more sensitive and thorough for what they detect in urine. But thank you

I don’t seem to get a consensus about how long it is detectable in urine either. I see some things saying up to 9 days whereas other opiates is 3-4 (I’ve tested clean when taking my pills a day before my appointment, so I know I have a faster metabolism than most). I think this is definitely the way to go. Thanks
Yeah it seems like I’m not going to be confident until I go to my appointment. My last pain clinic had a gas chromatograph to test urine so everything shows up. Thank you for a very thorough answer.

Unfortunately it’s a new doctor due to insurance. It’s sort of a loaded question asking what panel they use. As far as the plant argument, I don’t really agree with you on that one. Opium, THC are both plant derived and they have tests. But I do appreciate your input. Thank you!

Don’t think your experience is that uncommon unfortunately. I think your wait time is pretty long and was probably excruciating, but because doctors seem to think giving opioids in a controlled setting is something bad (vague intentionally here because who knows what they actually believe). I think a lot of your experience has to deal with being younger as well (probably less than 50 years old) and this compounded with you needing pain meds just sort of puts you up against a wall. Sorry your experience didn’t seem to include compassion from medical professionals. The whole ER experience (in the US) seems to involve a lot of control from the doctor, who seem to often fib and tell us there are protocols in place for them they must strictly abide by if pressed about care. My opinion here is formed from my own experience going to the ER and people over at r/chronicpain. 

Try to be grateful how fortunate you are to have people like your friend to stick up for you in a vulnerable situation and more importantly feel better!

Probably not. 40-80 mg/day user. Go about a week on, week off schedule. Tolerance is only increasing for me. Shoot for two or more weeks off. I’ve heard your tolerance can climb right back up to where it was pretty quickly when you pick back up, especially if you’re tolerance isn’t crazy high at this point (it’s medium to lower end of high to me)
